findings.issue: The FF-FCI12 meta-gate's is_sanctioned() only matches the {task,file} pair on a line; it does NOT validate the sanctioned_by or decision fields. T-0233's new entry is sanctioned_by:"mechanism" with decision:"ADR-T-0233-§6/§8-additive-allowlist" (not a founder_decide@DATE/sanctioned_by:"founder" as the file's own documented schema on lines 6/12 states). For THIS task the self-grant is legitimate under D-060 (additive thaw + narrow-unpark negative self-test = the auto-sanctionable class; widening is additive-only, frozen files untouched, narrow check verified). But the gate would equally accept a DESTRUCTIVE self-grant labelled mechanism with no founder trace — a latent provenance gap. Recommend the founder ratify the D-060 auto-sanction trace for audit completeness, and a follow-up harden is_sanctioned() to assert sanctioned_by/decision class (founder vs mechanism, additive vs destructive).
findings.suggestion: Founder: confirm the D-060 additive auto-sanction for T-0233 in the control-plane audit. Follow-up task: extend is_sanctioned() to validate sanctioned_by ∈ {founder,mechanism} and reject mechanism-class self-grants on destructive thaws.

findings.issue: The AC-2 test comment claims 'zero network calls' and constructs the stub with recordCalls:true, but never asserts stub.calls.length (or that the real adapter was not invoked). The zero-network guarantee is genuinely enforced elsewhere (precheck-no-network-in-core.sh + dormantLlmPort design + StubLlmPort being injected), so this is cosmetic, but the assertion text overstates what the test body checks.
findings.suggestion: Add expect(stub.calls.length).toBe(1) (and assert stub === injected port) to make the 'zero external network' claim self-evident in the test.

findings.issue: The stub's doc comment says 'Zero network: throws if the test environment has OPENAI_API_KEY set (safety check)', but complete() implements no such OPENAI_API_KEY guard. Doc/code mismatch — harmless (the stub never touches the network regardless), but the promised safety check is absent.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the OPENAI_API_KEY guard in the constructor, or remove the claim from the doc comment.

findings.issue: The (b) allowlist grep -vE 'appendAuditEvent|payload|reasoningTrace|traceRef|undefined|null|...' would also pass a hypothetical line that reads result.reasoning and assigns it elsewhere if that line happened to contain one of the allowlisted tokens. Not a real leak today (verified: run-precheck.ts:407-410 uses result.reasoning only to derive a random-UUID reasoningTraceRef; the reasoning text never reaches answer/outcome/res.json), but the grep is permissive enough that a future regression could slip through.
findings.suggestion: Tighten the egress check to assert .reasoning appears ONLY in the reasoningTraceRef derivation / appendAuditEvent payload, anchored more strictly than a token-allowlist.
